messages.author: 3f3060000990daa6
messages.subject: Offsetting objects on the x-axis
parts:
Hi all,

I tried to offset an object, so that it doesn't overlap others - here's a simple example:

ggplot(diamonds[1:1000,], aes(cut, carat)) + geom_point(alpha=0.3) + stat_summary(fun.data="mean_cl_normal", color="red")


I'd like to move the pointrange a bit to the right, so that the points are not overlapped - I tried position_dodge, etc. but it didn't work ...
Any ideas?

Thanks,
Felix

messages.author: 5ec5102a43e29af7
messages.subject: Re: Offsetting objects on the x-axis
parts:
Hi,

maybe like this:
ggplot(diamonds[1:1000,], aes(cut, carat)) +

geom_point(alpha=0.3,position=position_dodge(width=.2)) +
stat_summary(fun.data="mean_cl_normal",color="red")

regards,
stefan

messages.author: 223beb57ce203bde
messages.subject: Re: Offsetting objects on the x-axis
parts:
How about this:

df <- diamonds[1:1000,]
ggplot(df, aes(y = carat)) +
geom_point(aes(as.numeric(cut)), alpha=0.3) +
stat_summary(aes(as.numeric(cut)+0.2), fun.data="mean_cl_normal",
color="red") +
scale_x_continuous('cut', breaks = 1:nlevels(df$cut), labels =
levels(df$cut), minor_breaks = NA)

Xie Chao
